name: Yohannes Melese
headline: I build intelligence into working systems.
introduction: I'm an AI/ML engineer with a foundation in electronics, computer science, and competitive programming. My work connects research with the less glamorous details that make a system useful: evaluation, validation, reproducibility, and delivery.
perspective: I like problems where the model is only part of the answer. A document pipeline needs an audit trail. A language model needs an honest evaluation. A hardware implementation needs to respect the device it runs on.

projects.title: Documents → decisions you can inspect
projects.name: Tax Document Extraction Pipeline
projects.description: Tax returns arrive as inconsistent PDFs, scans, and supporting statements. I built a pipeline that combines OCR and deterministic extraction with an LLM fallback, then checks arithmetic identities before writing a workbook. Confidence-based review and a JSON audit trail keep the output inspectable.
projects.alt: Probe capture: fields on a tax page feed rules, LLM fallback, arithmetic check, and confidence channels; a low-confidence field is flagged for review.

projects.title: Parallel models. A hardware constraint.
projects.name: FPGA-Based Ensemble Neural Networks
projects.description: My master's research explored an ensemble of lightweight neural networks on FPGA hardware. I combined parallel execution, quantization, and a voting stage to investigate real-time inference. It brought model design and hardware implementation into the same engineering problem.
projects.alt: Timing capture: three parallel model lanes predict each cycle, and a majority vote registered on the next clock edge resolves their disagreements.

projects.title: A competition workflow, made scriptable
projects.name: Zindi CLI
projects.description: Moving between a competition page, datasets, submissions, and results interrupts an otherwise reproducible workflow. I built a Python CLI that connects those steps, with structured JSON output and typed failures for scripts and agents. The implementation is public, so you can inspect the engineering directly.
projects.alt: Console capture: a zindi-cli session where every command returns one JSON document, and an expired login exits with code 3.

research.title: African-language speech recognition
research.description: Combining recognizers for Lingala, Shona, and Luganda, with speaker-aware evaluation and language routing that cannot rely on hidden labels.

research.title: Multilingual health QA
research.description: Comparing baselines and LoRA adaptation for health questions in low-resource African languages, with language-specific evaluation.

research.title: Historical handwriting recognition
research.description: Adapting visual readers for seventeenth-century archives, preserving transcript provenance, replayable experiments, and negative findings.

foundations: **Toptal Verified Expert in Engineering.** AI/ML engineering and development for clients; previously led robotics and autonomous-systems R&D at Ethronics.
**M.Sc. Electronics Engineering, ASTU.** 4.00/4.00, University Topper. Dual-major B.Sc. in Electronics & Communication Engineering and Computer Science & Engineering; 3.98/4.00, Gold Medalist.
**Competitive programming → engineering discipline.** First place, Zindi UmojaHack Ethiopia (2021); EtCPC silver (2022) and bronze (2020).
background: Before these projects, I worked on Python development and training data at Turing, supported electronics research and laboratories at ASTU, and led data-science tutorials and programming contests at CSEC-ASTU. Teaching and team leadership remain part of how I work.
invitation: Working on an AI system, document automation, or hardware-aware ML? I'd be glad to hear about the problem, its constraints, and what a useful outcome would look like.
